Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the sentences in the right order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph.

A. When the secretary informed them that he would not be back soon, they left.

B. They seemed very agitated and wanted to meet him.

C. Some ladies gathered outside the Association President's office.

D. They waited for two hours.
questions.solution:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** While arranging the parts of the sentence, we have to find some grammatical or contextual relationships between them. So let's find them out.

__
 
• By reading the paragraph, we can understand the paragraph seems to be a report on what some ladies did.
 
 
• The first statement of a sentence in jumble-questions is usually **an independent general statement, a noun, a universal fact, or the starting of an incident**.

 Sentence **C **will come first as it is independent and it acts as the precursor to the sequence of events that happened next. This sentence introduces us to who the characters of the event were: this can be detected by the **use of nouns**. (*Some ladies__ gathered outside the __Association President's office__.*)

 __
 
• So it takes the **first place**.
 
 
 
• Next comes **B**; we can deduce this as the word '***they***' refers back to **the ladies** and '***him***' to the **Association President** mentioned in the previous sentence. (*They__ seemed very agitated and wanted to meet __him__*.)
 
 
• So it takes **second place**.
 
 
 
• After that will come **D** as it gives us more information about what the ladies did. (*They waited for two hours.*)
 
 
• So it takes** third place**.
 
 
 
• At last, will come sentence **A **where we can see how the whole thing ended. (*When the secretary informed them that he would not be back soon, they left.*)
 
 
• So here it will take the **final place**,
 
 
 
 
 
• Therefore, as per the points mentioned above, we find that the correct order is '**CBDA**'.

 

*So, the paragraph in the correct order is '**Some ladies gathered outside the Association President's office. They seemed very agitated and wanted to meet him. They waited for two hours. When the secretary informed them that he would not be back soon, they left.***'

questions.question:
Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the sentences in the correct order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph.

(A) Today, it is many times richer in industry, food and raw materials.

(B) Today, we have allies who jointly with us form a united front against the German invaders.

(C) Today, we enjoy the sympathy and support of all the peoples of Europe fallen under the yoke of Fascist tyranny.

(D) Today, our country is in a far better position that it was 23 years ago.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 3**.

__
 
• The paragraph should logically introduce an idea or situation and then provide elaboration and examples.
 
• **Sentence D** is the natural introductory sentence as it sets a comparative perspective between today and 23 years ago: "*Today, our country is in a far better position that it was 23 years ago.*"
 
• **Sentence A** should follow as it supports the introductory sentence by highlighting improvements in industry, food, and raw materials: "*Today, it is many times richer in industry, food and raw materials.*"
 
• **Sentence B** continues the explanation of today's advantageous position by mentioning the allied forces: "*Today, we have allies who jointly with us form a united front against the German invaders.*"
 
• **Sentence C** concludes by adding the support from European nations, further emphasizing the improved position: "*Today, we enjoy the sympathy and support of all the peoples of Europe fallen under the yoke of Fascist tyranny.*"

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 3**. The sentences should be arranged in the order **DABC**.

 

**Coherent paragraph after rearrangement:**

"*Today, our country is in a far better position that it was 23 years ago. Today, it is many times richer in industry, food and raw materials. Today, we have allies who jointly with us form a united front against the German invaders. Today, we enjoy the sympathy and support of all the peoples of Europe fallen under the yoke of Fascist tyranny.*"

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• **Option 2 (BCAD)** disrupts the logical flow by not starting with a general statement of the improved position and ending with a specific detail.

3p = q + r + s ---(1)

3q = p + r + s ---(2)

3(p - q) = q - p

⇒ p = q ---(3)

Adding equations (1) and (2)

3p + 3q = p + q + 2(r + s)

Also, The average weight of P and R is equal to the average weight of R and S

The sum of weights of P, Q, R, S, and T = 60 + 60 + 60 + 60 + 90 = 330 kgs

Average = 330/5 = 66 kgs

**∴ The average weight of all the containers together is 66 kgs.**

Radius of the circle, OA = 5 cm

questions.question: By selling an article for ₹20, a dealer makes a profit of 10%. By how much should he increase his selling price (in ₹, rounded off to two decimal place) so as to make a profit of 30%?

**∴ The correct answer is ₹3.64.**

⇒ Increase in SP = (260 ÷ 11) − 20

⇒ Increase in SP = (260 − 220) ÷ 11 = 40 ÷ 11

⇒ Increase in SP = 3.6363... ≈ ₹3.64

**∴ The correct answer is ₹3.64.**

Profit occurs when SP is greater than CP. Profit percentage is always calculated on the CP unless otherwise stated. Formula: Profit% = [(SP − CP) ÷ CP] × 100.

questions.question: The average score of 30 boys in a group test is recorded as 35. However, it was later discovered that two scores of 30 were mistakenly recorded as 40, and one score of 29 was incorrectly noted as 21. What is the correct average score of the group?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Average of 30 boys = 35

Incorrect entries: Two 30s recorded as 40, one 29 recorded as 21

**Formula used:**

Total actual sum = Average × Number of students

Corrected sum = Incorrect sum − Extra added + Missing amount

Correct average = Corrected sum ÷ 30

**Calculation:**

Total (wrong) sum = 35 × 30 = 1050

Error 1: 2 scores of 30 recorded as 40 ⇒ extra = (40 − 30) × 2 = 20

Error 2: 29 recorded as 21 ⇒ loss = 29 − 21 = 8

Corrected sum = 1050 − 20 + 8 = 1038

Correct average = 1038 ÷ 30 = 34.6

**∴ Correct average score = 34.6**

questions.question:
Consider the following statements and choose the correct option:

Statement (A): Tribal communities practiced jhum cultivation as a form of shifting agriculture.

Statement (B): The British encouraged jhum cultivation as it aligned with their economic policies.

Options:

options.text: Both (A) and (B) are true, and (B) is the reason for (A)
Both (A) and (B) are true, but (B) is not the reason for (A)

questions.solution:
**The correct answer is: c) (A) is true, but (B) is false.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

__
 
• **Statement (A): Tribal communities practiced jhum cultivation as a form of shifting agriculture.**

 
 
• This statement is **true**. Jhum cultivation, also known as shifting cultivation, was commonly practiced by tribal communities across different regions in India.
 
• In this agricultural method, a patch of forest is cleared, cultivated for a few years until the soil fertility decreases, and then left fallow as the community moves to a new area.
 
• It was a sustainable form of agriculture adapted to the environmental and cultural needs of many tribal communities.
 
 
 
• **Statement (B): The British encouraged jhum cultivation as it aligned with their economic policies.**
 
 
• This statement is **false**. The British discouraged jhum or shifting cultivation because it did not provide a steady revenue stream, which conflicted with their land revenue policies aimed at maximizing income from agriculture.
 
• The British preferred settled agriculture, which allowed them to impose fixed land taxes, leading them to often ban or restrict shifting cultivation practices, especially in forested regions.
 
 

**Therefore, Statement (A) is true, but Statement (B) is false.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Impact of British Policies on Jhum Cultivation:**__

 
 
• **Restrictions on Shifting Cultivation:** The British imposed various restrictions on jhum cultivation to encourage settled agriculture, which fit their tax collection model better.
 
• **Impact on Tribal Livelihoods:** These restrictions affected tribal communities’ traditional livelihoods, often leading to economic hardship and resistance against British policies.
 
• **Environmental Adaptation:** Jhum cultivation was an eco-friendly practice adapted to the forested and hilly terrains, and its restriction disrupted the ecological balance in some regions.

Ibn- Batuta came to India from __**Morocco**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• 
 **Ibn Battuta** was a **Moroccan traveller** who left his home at a young age of 21 back in the 13th century to travel across the world.
 
 
• 
 During his 30 years of travelling exploration, he** visited around 44 countries**, including** India.**
 
 
• 
 His travelling accounts are published in the book ‘**Rihla’ – My travels'**, a part of which is devoted to his experience in India.
 
 
• 
 **Ibn Battuta **came to** India in 1333 AD **through the high mountains of Afghanistan (**Hindu Kush Mountains**) and the **Indus river** on 12 September and made his way to Delhi at the time when the **Tughlaq dynasty** was at its height.
 
 
• 
 Upon his arrival in Sindh, Ibn Battuta mentions the Indian rhinoceros that lived on the banks of the Indus.
 
 
• 
 Crossing the Sutlej river in modern-day Pakistan, he paid obeisance at the shrine of **Baba Farid.**
 
 
• 
 From the **Rajput kingdom of Saraswati**, Battuta visited **Hansi** in India, describing it as among the most beautiful cities.
 
 
• 
 
Ibn Battuta reached the royal court of **Mohammad Bin Tughlaq**, the then ruler of Delhi, presented him with precious gifts and in return Battuta was given a furnished house, a job of **Qadi (Judge) **in the royal court by the king and stayed for around** seven years**. 

 

Hence, we can conclude that Ibn- Batuta came to India from Morocco__.
